messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: latency_slo.breach for /v1/decode (p99 > 800ms) — region: eu-west-1 — current_p99=1234ms — triggered at 2026-04-03T02:00:10Z :rotating_light:

jordan: @incident-bot seeing the page. i'm on it. starting a triage, assigning maya for metrics/console, kai for recent deploys.

maya: grabbing dashboards — p95 spiked from ~120ms -> 410ms, p99 to 1.2s. 99th token stalls visible in streaming traces.

kai: I rolled out the runtime kernel update (trt/flash-attn v2) at 01:45 UTC in eu-west-1. short canary, then 100% at 01:54. no errors in CI.

arvind: saw increased decode tail in canary but not flagged in alerts. letting it run was my call.

jordan: ok let's collect evidence. maya can you paste the flamegraph and last 1h sample?

maya: flamegraph: top shows hot: decode_loop -> nv_decode_kernel -> flash_attn_kernel. tail latency lines spike around 01:55. streaming stalls show last-token wait > 700ms.

maya: metrics snippet:
```
agg.decode.p95{route="/v1/decode",region="eu-west-1"} 410
agg.decode.p99{route="/v1/decode",region="eu-west-1"} 1234
streaming.stalls.count{region="eu-west-1"} 87
gpu.utilization{pool="decode-eu"} 68
```

kai: suspects: the new TRT kernels' workspace allocation interacts poorly with our per-request KV cache fallback, causing stalls when cache misses happen. also one compiler flag changed: COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL=3 -> COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL=4 in the build profile.

sofia: customers impacted list (top 3): ingest-ai (latency-sensitive), chatflow-pro (streaming clients), search-saas (batch less impacted). notifying CS.

jordan: immediate mitigation plan (quick bullets):
1) route 20% traffic away from eu-west-1 to eu-central for /v1/decode via smart-routing.
2) revert runtime kernels in eu-west-1 to previous build (rollback).
3) if rollback not feasible quickly, disable flash-attn path via runtime env override.
4) raise streaming timeout to reduce incomplete streams and give clients better failover.

kai: starting step 1 now — updating router policy.

kai: command run:
```
redwood-routerctl set-policy --route "/v1/decode" --region-balance eu-west-1=80,eu-central=20 --reason "latency spike eu-west-1"
```

maya: after moving 20% traffic — p99 eu-west-1 dropped from 1234ms -> 970ms, overall region traffic p99 improved slightly. but still over SLO.

kai: rolling back kernel pod set in eu-west-1:
```
kubectl -n runtime rollout undo ds/decode-gpu --to-revision=25
```

kai: rollback started. watching pods come up.

arvind: note — the rollback will keep the new compiler-compiled model artifacts; we might need to invalidate cache if binary layouts differ. prepping cache flush script.

jordan: if rollback fails, do step 3. how long for rollback? estimate 4-6min to get healthy pods.

infra-oncall: watch node gpu scheduling — one node OOMed during canary, restarted. verifying node stability.

sofia: CS update draft: "We're investigating increased tail latency for decode in eu-west-1. Engineers have mitigations in progress (traffic routing + rollback). We'll post updates every 15m." pinging customers. :thumbsup:

maria (customer-ops-bot): sent update to ingest-ai and chatflow-pro, both acknowledged and requested ETA.

kai: rollback finished at 02:08:32Z. pods are Ready=6/6.

maya: post-rollback metrics (02:10 snapshot):
```
agg.decode.p95{region="eu-west-1"} 150
agg.decode.p99{region="eu-west-1"} 220
streaming.stalls.count{region="eu-west-1"} 3
```

arvind: that's a solid improvement. confirms new kernel was the cause.

jordan: great — restore full traffic to eu-west-1 but keep alerts on and continue 1h of elevated monitoring. run a canary with the kernel patch but with COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL=3 instead of 4 and instrument memory allocations.

kai: creating a patch branch and will build patch with COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL=3 and flash-attn v2 disabled-by-default.

kai: build command (for CI):
```
export COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL=3
export TRT_FLASH_ATTENTION=0
make build-runtime-kernel && ci/publish-kernel --canary
```

arvind: also we should add a regression test: synthetic streaming workload with forced KV cache miss patterns to catch stalls. I'll draft test today.

jordan: handoff notes for next oncall (maya):
- incident started 02:00Z, root cause: runtime kernel change (trt/flash-attn + compiler opt level) increased decode tail latency in eu-west-1.
- mitigations: router shifted 20% traffic -> eu-central, then kernel rollback completed 02:08Z.
- customer impact: transient SLO breach p99 ~1.2s, affected customers notified.
- followups: kai to land safe rebuild with OPT=3 and flash-attn disabled-by-default; arvind to add regression test; infra to vet OOM node that restarted during canary.
- postmortem owner: jordan. draft due EOD tomorrow.

maya: i'll keep monitoring dashboards for the next 60m and will escalate if any regression reappears. handing off to you @oncall-next.

jordan: thanks team. tags for PM/CS: @sofia please coordinate customer followups and any credits if needed.

infra-oncall: noted — i'm going to run node diagnostics for the restarted GPU and check driver versions (matching pre-rollback baseline).

sofia: acknowledged. i'll coordinate comms.

jordan: closing the page for now — keep thread open for follow-ups. good job moving fast and safe. :tada:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — latency_slo.breach cleared at 2026-04-03T02:12:50Z. duration 12m40s.
